notes: Hand-derived before the detector ran, from the normalisation in crates/codemap/src/ruby_lex.rs: names are $id, literals are $lit (a string is one token: its opening quote), keywords and punctuation stay, comments and newlines leave no token. A group's occurrences are the method's own lines because every twin sits between different neighbours in the two files, so no token run reaches past the method: before `def summarise` a.rb has `$lit` ("set") and b.rb `end`; after its `end` a.rb has `def` and b.rb `$id` (Marker); before `def tally` a.rb has `end` and b.rb `$lit` (3); after its `end` a.rb has `$id` (NEAR) and b.rb `def`.
summarise: verbatim in both files (Type-1). 17 lines each; one comment-only line and one blank line inside, so 15 source lines; 56 tokens.
tally / count_up: same shape, every identifier and literal changed (Type-2). 16 lines, all source; 58 tokens (the raise line adds eight so the run is not at the threshold).
near_tokens_a / near_tokens_b: `def $id ( $id` then `)` against `,`; the shared `$id = $lit $id . $id do | $id |` inside is nine tokens: under the 50-token threshold, no group.

wide: verbatim in both files and over 50 tokens (thirty literals and their commas), but four lines: under the 5-line threshold, no group. Its neighbours differ (`end` against `)` before, `def` against `$id` after) so no run carries it to five.
